Alger, 25 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 25, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — A recent study by Kaspersky's research center reveals a higher awareness among women regarding the real impacts of digital violence. Published ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the survey highlights differing opinions on how to handle these threats.
Un impact physique et psychologique plus: A physical and psychological impact more feared by women
Une enquête menée par le Centre de reche: A survey conducted by Kaspersky's internal marketing research center highlights the differing perceptions between women and men regarding tech-facilitated violence. These abuses notably include cyberstalking, malicious surveillance, digital manipulation, and the dissemination of content aimed at intimidating or controlling an individual.
Les résultats montrent que les femmes so: The results show that more women anticipate the real physical repercussions of these attacks. Thus, 55% of female respondents identify risks of escalation in daily life, physical assaults, or stress-related health problems, compared to 48% of men. Moreover, 81% of women recognize psychological impacts such as trauma or depression, compared to 77% of men.
Une divergence sur la responsabilité et: A divergence on responsibility and institutional response
La prise en charge de ces menaces numéri: The management of these digital threats draws contrasting views. Indeed, 44% of women state that combating this violence is a societal issue requiring regulation and public action, compared to 36% of men. Conversely, 21% of men believe that online security is primarily an individual responsibility, a position shared by 15% of women.
Selon Tatyana Shishkova, responsable par: According to Tatyana Shishkova, acting head within Kaspersky's GReAT team, access to geolocation and connected devices allows abusers to track victims' real-world activities, blurring the line between digital and physical harm. Meanwhile, Dr. Leonie Maria Tanczer from University College London advocates for a global response combining legislation, safe technology design, and institutional support. To help users, Kaspersky offers a checklist to detect surveillance software on iOS and Android devices.
